page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Molality
lines: Molality (m) is the number of moles of solute
dissolved in one kilogram of SOLVENT.

lines.text: m = moles of solute / mass of solvent in kg

steps.why: Molality is defined per kilogram of solvent, not per litre of solution — that one word is the entire difference from molarity, and it makes molality independent of temperature.
common_mistakes: Writing 'per kilogram of solution'. The denominator is the SOLVENT alone.
Confusing molality m with molarity M.
steps.memory_tip: MolaLity goes with kiLograms of soLvent; molaRity goes with litRes of solution.
steps.margin_note: The word solvent and the unit mol kg⁻¹ carry this mark.

steps.label: Mole fraction
lines: Mole fraction of a component is its number of
moles divided by the total moles in the mixture.

lines.text: x₁ = n₁ / (n₁ + n₂) ; x₁ + x₂ = 1 ; no unit

steps.why: A fraction of the total mole count needs no unit, and the fractions of all components must add to 1 — both properties follow directly from the definition.
common_mistakes: Dividing by the OTHER component's moles instead of the total.
Attaching a unit. A mole fraction is a pure number.
steps.memory_tip: Part over whole: one component's moles over everyone's moles, and all the fractions sum to 1.
steps.margin_note: The sum-to-1 property is the standard follow-up — state it unprompted.

insider_note: Two definitions, one mark each, and each turns on its denominator: the solvent alone for molality, the total moles for mole fraction. Adding the unit to one and stating that the other has none closes both marks.
